title: Searching for MobileNetV3
authors: Andrew Howard, Mark Sandler, Grace Chu, Liang-Chieh Chen, Bo Chen, Mingxing Tan, Weijun Wang, Yukun Zhu, Ruoming Pang, Vijay Vasudevan, Quoc V. Le, Hartwig Adam
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
conclusions: Introduces MobileNetV3-Large and MobileNetV3-Small, found by combining hardware-aware platform-specific NAS (MnasNet-style) with the NetAdapt layer-wise search algorithm
Adds new architecture-level efficiency improvements: redesigned expensive first/last layers, and the h-swish nonlinearity (a piecewise-linear, quantization-friendly approximation of swish)
MobileNetV3-Large is 3.2% more accurate than MobileNetV2 at 20% lower latency on Pixel phones; MobileNetV3-Small is 6.6% more accurate than a comparable MobileNetV2 model
Proposes Lite R-ASPP (LR-ASPP), a new efficient segmentation decoder built on MobileNetV3, giving faster mobile semantic segmentation at similar/better accuracy on Cityscapes
Reports detection (COCO, SSDLite) and segmentation (Cityscapes) results showing MobileNetV3 backbones dominate the accuracy/latency Pareto frontier versus MobileNetV2, MnasNet, and ProxylessNAS
Ablates individual components (h-swish placement, squeeze-and-excite bottleneck ratio, NetAdapt) to show each contributes measurable latency/accuracy gains
our_use: main.tex:347 -- 'The headline grid uses three backbones, MobileNetV3 \citep{howard2019searching}, RegNetY-400MF \citep{radosavovic2020designing}, and a ViT-B/16 transformer \citep{dosovitskiy2021image}, to show the findings are not CNN-specific.' Purely an attribution citation naming the architecture used as one of the paper's backbones -- no substantive claim about the method's contents beyond identifying the source of the architecture.
